cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still speaking to all Israel (Deuteronomy 5:1), laying out laws for the land the LORD is giving them. First up, marriage: if a man finds some indecency in his wife, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her and send her away. Now say she marries another man, and that marriage ends too, by divorce or by his death.

cards.question: A divorced woman marries again, and that second marriage ends. Why does Moses say her first husband may not marry her again?

answers.text: It is an abomination to the LORD
Her second husband's family has a claim
The elders must approve it first

cards.text: Next up, newlyweds. For one year, a newly married man must not be sent to war or pressed into any duty.

cards.question: A newlywed gets a whole year with no war and no duty. What is he free to do with it?

answers.text: Stay home and bring joy to his wife
Serve the priests at the tabernacle
Build a new house for his family

cards.text: The closest I ever got to time off was years in the back of a junk drawer, and NOBODY was bringing anybody joy in there. Next, loans: a lender must not take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper one, as security for a debt.

cards.question: Why can't a lender take a man's millstones as security for a debt?

answers.text: It would take his livelihood as security
Millstones belong to the whole town
They are too heavy to carry off

cards.text: Then a hard one: if a man is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die.
Then infectious skin diseases: Israel must carefully follow everything the Levitical priests instruct.

cards.question: On skin diseases, Moses tells Israel to remember what the LORD did to someone on the journey out of Egypt. Who?

answers.text: Miriam
Aaron
Korah

cards.text: Back to loans. When you lend your neighbor something, you don't go into his house to collect security. You stand outside while he brings it out to you, and if he's poor, you don't go to sleep with it in your possession.

cards.question: Moses says a lender must return a poor man's security by sunset. Why?

answers.text: So he can sleep in his own cloak
So he can work the next morning
So he can repay the loan sooner

cards.question: True or false: Moses says giving the poor man's security back will be credited as righteousness before the LORD.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Moses keeps going, and now it's payday. Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says this protection is only for poor hired hands who are Israelites.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: When does Moses say a poor hired hand must be paid?

answers.text: Each day before sunset
At the end of each week
When the harvest is in

cards.question: Why does Moses say a hired hand's pay can't wait?

answers.text: He depends on it to get by
He might quit for other work
His master might forget the debt

cards.text: Hold it back, and he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you'll be guilty of sin. So not "the check's in the mail," not "next Friday," friend, it's TODAY, TODAY, TODAY!

cards.question: Moses turns to justice. When someone is put to death for sin, whose sin does he say it must be?

answers.text: His own sin
His father's sin
His children's sin

cards.text: Moses goes on: do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow's cloak as security.

cards.question: What reason does Moses give Israel for treating the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow this way?

answers.text: They were once slaves in Egypt
Foreigners bring trade to their towns
Widows can take them to the elders

cards.text: Harvest time: if you forget a sheaf in the field, don't go back for it, and don't go over the olive branches or the grapevines a second time. What's left is for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow.

cards.question: Leave the forgotten sheaf, so the LORD your God may ___ you in all the work of your hands.

answers.text: bless
test
judge

cards.text: And Moses brings back that reminder: remember you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That's why he's commanding all this.
Next, the courtroom. Disputes go before a judge, and if the guilty man deserves a beating, he gets the number of lashes his crime warrants, but no more than forty.

cards.question: Why does Moses cap a guilty man's beating at forty lashes?

answers.text: So their brother isn't degraded
So the judge can hear more cases
So the punishment ends by sunset

cards.question: Moses gives a law about an ox while it's treading out the grain. What must Israel not do to it?

answers.text: Muzzle it
Yoke it with a donkey
Sell it to a foreigner

cards.text: Now a family law: when brothers live together and one dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow.

cards.question: A man dies without a son, and his brother marries the widow. Why does their first son carry on the dead brother's name?

answers.text: So his name isn't blotted out from Israel
So the widow can keep her husband's house
So the elders can count him in the tribe

cards.question: A man won't marry his brother's widow, so she goes to the elders at the city gate. What does she tell them?

answers.text: He refuses to preserve his brother's name
He has taken her husband's field
He won't let her glean his harvest

cards.text: The elders summon him and speak with him. If he still says, “I do not want to marry her,” she removes his sandal in front of them and spits in his face.

cards.question: In front of the elders, the widow removes the brother's sandal. What does she declare?

answers.text: This is for the man who won't keep his brother's line
This is for the man who took his brother's land
This is for the man who broke his word to the elders

cards.text: From then on, his family name in Israel will be called “The House of the Unsandaled.”
Then a law about a fight. If a wife tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the attacker's genitals, her hand is to be cut off, with no pity shown.

Then business: no two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light, and no two differing measures in your house. That's like me keeping a BIG scoop for buying chocolate chips and a tiny scoop for selling them, and friend, that's not a recipe, that's a SCHEME.

cards.question: Moses says Israel must keep accurate and honest weights and measures. Why?

answers.text: So they may live long in the land
So the priests get a fair tithe
So the king can tax them fairly

cards.question: True or false: Moses says everyone who is dishonest with weights and measures is detestable to the LORD.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then Moses brings up the Amalekites, who attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17:8). They met Israel on the journey from Egypt, when everyone was tired and weary.

cards.question: Israel is tired and weary on the road. Who do the Amalekites attack?

answers.text: The stragglers at the back
The priests carrying the ark
The leaders at the front

cards.question: Moses says the Amalekites who attacked Israel on the road had no ___ of God.

answers.text: fear
love
word

cards.text: Moses says that when the LORD gives Israel rest from their enemies in the land, they are to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. “Do not forget!” And friend, Moses has more to say, so stick around.
